questions.prompt: The wise fear nothing, but the foolish tremble at every shadow.
questions.answer: Sapientēs nihil timent, sed stultī ad omnem umbram tremunt.

questions.prompt: The Greeks conquered the Trojans by cunning rather than by strength.
questions.answer: Graecī Trōiānōs dolō potius quam vīribus vīcērunt.

questions.prompt: The brave often help the weak in war.
questions.answer: Fortēs saepe īnfirmōs in bellō adiuvant.

questions.prompt: Small things delight boys, but great things attract kings.
questions.answer: Parva puerōs dēlectant, magna autem rēgēs alliciunt.

questions.prompt: The gods know all things, both the true and the false.
questions.answer: Dī omnia sciunt, et vēra et falsa.

questions.prompt: Many desire great things, few endure hard things.
questions.answer: Multī magna cupiunt, paucī dūra patiuntur.

questions.prompt: Time reveals hidden things and overthrows the mighty.
questions.answer: Tempus occulta aperit et magnōs ēvertit.

questions.prompt: This wise man envies no one, although he owns little.
questions.answer: Hīc sapiēns nēminī invidet, quamquam parva possidet.

questions.prompt: A certain learned man wrote many books about the stars.
questions.answer: Doctus quīdam multōs librōs dē astrīs scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The honest man, content with little, harms nobody.
questions.answer: Probus, parvō contentus, nēminī nocet.

questions.prompt: A Roman man does not fear death for his country.
questions.answer: Vir Rōmānus mortem prō patriā nōn timet.

questions.prompt: The learned praise the ancients, the unlearned scorn them.
questions.answer: Doctī veterēs laudant, indoctī contemnunt.

questions.prompt: Our men fought bravely while the enemy were fleeing.
questions.answer: Nostrī fortiter pugnāvērunt dum hostēs fugiunt.

questions.prompt: The rich, forgetful of the gods, often neglect the poor.
questions.answer: Dīvitēs, deōrum immemorēs, pauperēs saepe neglegunt.

questions.prompt: The good obey the laws; the wicked scorn them.
questions.answer: Bonī lēgibus pārent, malī eās contemnunt.

questions.prompt: The wise poet compares great things with small ones in his song.
questions.answer: Sapiēns poēta magna parvīs in carmine compōnit.

questions.prompt: Nature has hidden many things from mortals.
questions.answer: Nātūra multa ā mortālibus occultāvit.

questions.prompt: New things delight the crowd, old things delight the learned.
questions.answer: Nova vulgus dēlectant, vetera doctōs.

questions.prompt: This brave man defended his country against many foes.
questions.answer: Hīc fortis patriam contrā multōs dēfendit.

questions.prompt: A certain foolish man believed the false rather than the true.
questions.answer: Stultus quīdam falsa potius quam vēra crēdidit.

questions.prompt: The learned man teaches useful things, the orator pleasant ones.
questions.answer: Vir doctus ūtilia docet, ōrātor iūcunda.

questions.prompt: The immortals grant good things to the pious.
questions.answer: Immortālēs bona piīs tribuunt.
